summary: 40-foot L-4 pole tower built 1936 in the Kaniksu National Forest; destroyed in the 1967 Trapper Peak Fire; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1967 Trapper Peak Fire

events.note: Destroyed in the Trapper Peak Fire; Forest Lookouts says burned in a wildfire

evidence.supports: 40-foot pole L-4 tower built 1936; destroyed in Trapper Peak fire 1967
evidence.quote: 1936: 40' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed in Trapper Peak fire 1967.

evidence.quote: 5 miles north of Upper Priest Lake

evidence.supports: Trapper Peak Fire: lightning in northwest Boundary County, 31 days, 16,000 acres

evidence.supports: the lightning-caused fire is named the Trapper Peak Fire
evidence.quote: This fire, known as the Trapper Peak Fire

evidence.supports: listed as gone on the Idaho list

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Idaho list gives 48.88155, -116.90550, the same as the current record point. Idaho Fire Lookouts shows no coordinates on the page read, so the other point in the record (48.88002, -116.91297) has no source in this research.
Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say destroyed in the Trapper Peak Fire. The Forest Lookouts page says burned in a wildfire. All three give 1967, so they describe the same loss.

notes_for_editor: Build year and design come from two register sites (firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts) that may share a source; no agency record was read. Height 12.2 m is the 40-foot pole converted; the brief had no height. The Trapper Peak Fire is confirmed by the Boundary County Museum, but no source places the lookout inside the burn or names its exact spot. The Forest Lookouts page gives the legal location 64N-4W-19, not checked against the coordinates. One search for an independent Green Bonnet record found nothing. The Kaniksu National Forest or the Boundary County Museum may hold a file. Today's site condition is not in any source read.
